q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: WITH DUPLICATES AS ( SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(*) FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ) SELECT EMAIL FROM DUPLICATES
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: WITH DUPLICATES AS ( SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(*) FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ) SELECT EMAIL FROM DUPLICATES
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 does not use a CTE (Common Table Expression) and instead tries to group by the EMAIL column directly in the HAVING clause, which is not the intended behavior. Q2 correctly uses a CTE to first identify duplicates and then selects the EMAILs from this CTE. The difference in logic leads to different results when the PERSON table contains duplicate EMAILs.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should contain at least two rows with the same EMAIL, and another row with a unique EMAIL. The presence of duplicate EMAILs should trigger a difference in the results between Q1 and Q2.
